patterns.source: project/paper.txt (the source project's own paper, used as a same-genre structural exemplar; no external corpus available under the no-web constraint, AR-003)
patterns.rhetorical_purpose: Let a reader compare four otherwise-unrelated benchmark tasks on equal footing, and let each task's design choices be checked against a stated reason.
move_sequence: orient with one summary table across all four tasks (Table 1)
for each task: state why the task matters (a 'Rational' move) before any data/model detail
then how the pass/fail quality target was set, tied back to a measured reference number
patterns.reader_question_answered: Why does this specific task belong in the suite, and how was its pass/fail bar chosen (not just what the bar is)?
patterns.assumed_knowledge: General ML task/dataset/model vocabulary; not the specific datasets or prior TinyML models named
patterns.transition_behavior: Each of the four subsections repeats the same four-move template, so the reader's expectation, once set by the first subsection, carries over without needing to be re-explained.
patterns.evidence_placement: The quality-target rationale always cites a specific measured number (e.g., a reference-model accuracy) immediately before stating the chosen threshold, so the threshold reads as derived rather than arbitrary.
patterns.result_interpretation_pattern: State the measured number, then the threshold set from it, then (usually in one clause) the reason for the gap between them (e.g., 'to accommodate quantization differences').
patterns.figure_table_integration: Table 1 is placed before any subsection and is referred to implicitly (each subsection fills in one column); it is not a Figure/Table this paper reprints as an image, but its column structure is reused as this new paper's own comparison table.
patterns.signature: task rationale -> dataset -> model -> quality target, repeated per task, each target tied to a stated reference number
patterns.reader_effect: Four dissimilar tasks (audio, vision x2, anomaly detection) read as one coherent design method rather than four separate reports.

patterns.rhetorical_purpose: Give the reader the vocabulary and constraints needed to judge why prior benchmarks fall short, before naming those prior benchmarks.
move_sequence: name each challenge as a short label (Low Power, Limited Memory, Hardware Heterogeneity, Software Heterogeneity, Cross-product)
give one concrete consequence per challenge
only then move to Related Work, where each prior benchmark is shown failing on one or more of these named challenges
patterns.reader_question_answered: What would even count as a solution here, before being told what does not solve it?
patterns.assumed_knowledge: General systems/ML background; not TinyML-specific hardware constraints
patterns.transition_behavior: Related Work's critique of CoreMark/MLMark/MLPerf Inference reuses the exact challenge labels just introduced, so the reader recognizes the criteria rather than meeting new ones.
patterns.evidence_placement: Background concepts are front-loaded as their own section rather than folded into the Introduction, keeping the Introduction's orientation paragraph short.
patterns.signature: name the evaluation criteria before naming the things being evaluated against them
patterns.reader_effect: The Gap paragraph that follows reads as a checklist failure rather than an assertion the reader has to take on faith.
